why: Explorer loads the shell extension in its own process, so a defect there costs the operator their file browser rather than one viewer window. The release DLL therefore stays on the last revision verified in Explorer while the viewer moves on.
retire_when: The shell built from the current tree has been used in Explorer on a real machine through the thumbnail, preview-pane, file-association and uninstall paths, and nothing in the pin-to-HEAD delta for the crates above is still wanted.
backport: A fix that matters to Explorer (a parser, thumbnail, or COM defect) is cherry-picked onto the pinned revision and the pin moves forward to the new commit; the pin never moves to a revision that has not been exercised in Explorer.
check: scripts/report-shell-pin.sh writes the delta between this revision and the tree being released; the release records it as dist/occluview-shell-revision.json.
